rationale_short: KYT is named as a product to "Monitor transactions in real-time" with continuous screening of crypto transactions, corroborated by wu2023tracer naming Chainalysis as a forensics service performing tracing (T_indep).

Vendor describes "sophisticated machine learning with hundreds of clustering heuristics" and "AI-powered fraud prevention through Alterya" but names no GNN architecture (GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT), only generic clustering (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Neither vendor pages nor narrative nor any cross-platform source linked to P01 mention ZK proofs, Groth16, PLONK, STARK, Bulletproofs, or zero-knowledge circuits in connection with Chainalysis (T_vendor: absence).

Chainalysis vendor pages name Hexagate for exploit/scam prevention and Reactor for tracing, but do not document MEV (sandwich, front-running, JIT, arbitrage) detection categories, and no cross-platform source ties Chainalysis to MEV analytics (T_vendor: absence).

Vendor lists named products (KYT, Reactor, Sentinel, Address Screening) as discrete capabilities indicating programmatic delivery, but no REST/GraphQL endpoint family or auth scheme is documented in the available pages (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Vendor names "Token Monitoring: Smart contract scam and liquidity analysis" and analyst piece mentions wash trading is related to MEV bots, but neither names a specific MEV strategy category (sandwich, JIT) within Solidus's HALO (T_vendor primary).

Solidus vendor materials describe HALO as "trade surveillance, transaction monitoring, KYC intelligence, case management" with no FATF Recommendation 16 / Travel Rule originator-beneficiary VASP messaging capability mentioned (T_vendor: absence).

Narrative tags "Technical approach: ML, Anomaly" and vendor mentions "behavioral analytics" but no graph or GNN framing appears anywhere; HALO's spoofing/layering detection is described via "order book analysis" not graph methods (T_vendor: absence).

Vendor explicitly names "Transaction Monitoring: multidimensional screening of deposits and withdrawals across fiat and crypto" within HALO, corroborated by Solidus's own widely-reposted wash-trading methodology report scanning ~30,000 DEX pools (T_indep analyst piece + narrative).

No mention of W3C Verifiable Credentials, DIDs, SD-JWT, or attestation schemas in Solidus vendor or narrative materials; the platform is a market-surveillance tool with no credential layer (T_vendor: absence).

Lossless Aegis is named with "Automated real-time freezing of suspicious transactions" and "3+ billion scanned transactions" but no third-party paper, regulator, or analyst piece in the shared dossier references Lossless monitoring (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Vendor describes generic "Web3 security" with LERC-20 token freezing but does not name supported DeFi protocols (Uniswap, Aave, Curve, etc.) nor a contract-call semantic decoding framework; narrative section on DeFi semantic interpretation is context not attestation (T_vendor: absence).

Lossless materials describe stake-based community reporting and exploit freezing but contain no reference to MEV strategies (sandwich, arbitrage, JIT, liquidation) or MEV detection categories (T_vendor: absence).

Lossless homepage describes Aegis, Protocol, Token Minter & Vault Protection products but lists no developer API, SDK, REST/GraphQL endpoint, or programmatic access channel — the freeze mechanism appears to be on-chain via LERC-20 (T_vendor: absence).

Narrative explicitly tags "Technical approach: Heuristic, Governance" and vendor describes community/stake-based reporting with no ML or graph claims; nothing in the shared dossier suggests GNN use (T_vendor: absence).

Veriscope vendor page documents "the only frictionless Crypto Travel Rule compliance solution" with named counterparty VASPs (Binance, Bitfinex, Huobi, Gate.io), corroborated by Notabene's industry survey naming Shyft in the Travel Rule vendor cohort (T_indep).

Vendor positions Shyft as "a global attestation and governance platform" with "patented security mechanisms" and DLA Piper-attested due diligence, but no reference to W3C VC, DID, or SD-JWT credential schemas (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Shyft vendor materials describe identity validation, OAuth2-style consent, and VASP-to-VASP PII transmission via Veriscope but name no transaction-monitoring product, alert categories, or surveillance pipeline (T_vendor: absence).

Veriscope's "VASP-to-VASP customer data transfer" with "Pay-As-You-Go Model" and "historic transaction lookbacks" implies a programmatic interface but no REST/GraphQL endpoint family or authentication scheme is documented (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Shyft Network materials are entirely focused on identity attestations and Travel Rule messaging with no reference to MEV strategies, sandwich attacks, or extractable-value detection (T_vendor: absence).

Vendor AML page explicitly lists "Suspicious Transaction Activity Reporting (STAR)" alongside SAM and KYC as a named AML solution, but no peer-reviewed paper, regulator filing, or analyst report in the shared dossier benchmarks NICE Actimize's SAR template (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Vendor names "Currency Transaction Reporting (CTR)" as a discrete AML solution alongside SAM and Sanctions Screening, a US-specific FinCEN report format, but no T_indep source corroborates NICE's CTR filing pipeline (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Vendor names "Suspicious Activity Monitoring (SAM)" with "5 billion+ transactions monitored daily" and "$6 trillion protected each day", and the SoK narrative explicitly classifies NICE Actimize as "Primary function: Tx Monitoring" with rule-based + ML technical approach (T_indep narrative + vendor scale).

Narrative tags "Technical approach: Rule-Based, ML" and vendor positions "entity-centric AML solutions, infused with AI and machine learning" with no graph or GNN architecture mentioned; NICE is a traditional rule-engine + tabular ML platform (T_vendor: absence).

NICE Actimize materials cover AML/KYC/SAM/CTR for traditional finance with no reference to FATF Recommendation 16, originator-beneficiary VASP messaging, or any crypto-specific Travel Rule integration (T_vendor: absence).
